title: Errori tipici: B2
intro: Errori sottili che restano anche a livello avanzato: inversioni, preposizioni dopo verbi e aggettivi, collocazioni e falsi amici.

items.wrong: I have lived in Rome until 2015.
items.right: I lived in Rome until 2015.
items.why: Un periodo chiuso nel passato, con un termine preciso, vuole il past simple. In italiano «ho vissuto» funziona.
alts: I lived in Rome up to 2015.
more: I living in Rome until 2015.

items.wrong: Hardly I had arrived when it started to rain.
items.right: Hardly had I arrived when it started to rain.
items.why: Dopo avverbi negativi come «hardly» all'inizio si inverte ausiliare e soggetto. L'italiano non ha questa inversione.
more: Hardly had I arrived than it started to rain.

items.wrong: Never I have seen such a mess.
items.right: Never have I seen such a mess.
items.why: «Never» a inizio frase richiede l'inversione ausiliare + soggetto. In italiano «mai ho visto» non inverte.
more: Never have I saw such a mess.

items.wrong: She is capable to solve the problem.
items.right: She is capable of solving the problem.
items.why: «Capable» regge «of» + gerundio. L'italiano «capace di risolvere» porta a «to + infinito».
more: She is capable of solve the problem.

items.wrong: He insisted to pay for dinner.
items.right: He insisted on paying for dinner.
items.why: «Insist» vuole «on» + gerundio. In italiano «insistere nel pagare» ha l'infinito.
more: He insisted on pay for dinner.

items.wrong: They prevented me to enter.
items.right: They prevented me from entering.
items.why: «Prevent someone» vuole «from» + gerundio. L'italiano «impedirmi di entrare» ha l'infinito.
more: They prevented me from enter.

items.wrong: I object to be treated like this.
items.right: I object to being treated like this.
items.why: «Object to» vuole il gerundio, perché «to» è una preposizione. Si scambia con l'infinito.
more: I object being treated like this.

items.wrong: If I would have known, I would have told you.
items.right: If I had known, I would have told you.
items.why: Nel terzo condizionale la frase con «if» vuole il past perfect, non «would». In italiano si dice «se avessi saputo», e la tentazione è «would».
alts: Had I known, I would have told you.
more: If I had known, I would told you.

items.wrong: He asked if could he borrow my car.
items.right: He asked if he could borrow my car.
items.why: Nelle domande indirette l'ordine è soggetto + verbo, senza inversione. Si trascina l'ordine della domanda diretta.
more: He asked if he can borrowed my car.

items.wrong: The news are worrying.
items.right: The news is worrying.
items.why: «News» ha la «-s» ma è non numerabile e singolare. In italiano «le notizie» è plurale.
more: The new is worrying.

items.wrong: She is responsible of the accounts.
items.right: She is responsible for the accounts.
items.why: «Responsible» regge «for». L'italiano «responsabile di» porta a «of».
more: She is responsible to the accounts.

items.wrong: He is jealous for my success.
items.right: He is jealous of my success.
items.why: «Jealous» regge «of». L'errore tipico è tradurre «geloso di» con «for».
more: He is jealous to my success.

items.wrong: I did a mistake in the report.
items.right: I made a mistake in the report.
items.why: La collocazione corretta è «make a mistake». L'italiano «fare un errore» usa «fare» per tutto.
more: I made a mistakes in the report.

items.wrong: I have a great experience in sales.
items.right: I have a lot of experience in sales.
items.why: «Experience» nel senso di esperienza professionale è non numerabile e si quantifica con «a lot of». In italiano si dice «una grande esperienza».
alts: I have lots of experience in sales.
I have a great deal of experience in sales.
I have plenty of experience in sales.
I have extensive experience in sales.
more: I have a lot of experiences in sales.

items.wrong: Could you please to confirm your attendance?
items.right: Could you please confirm your attendance?
items.why: Dopo «could» (e «please») il verbo è all'infinito senza «to». Si aggiunge «to» per analogia con l'italiano «potrebbe per favore confermare».
more: Could you please confirming your attendance?

items.wrong: Despite he was tired, he kept working.
items.right: Although he was tired, he kept working.
items.why: «Despite» è una preposizione: vuole un nome o un gerundio, non una frase. Con una frase si usa «although».
alts: Despite being tired, he kept working.
In spite of being tired, he kept working.
Despite the fact that he was tired, he kept working.
Even though he was tired, he kept working.
more: Despite of being tired, he kept working.

items.wrong: It's time we go home.
items.right: It's time we went home.
items.why: Dopo «it's time» + soggetto si usa il past simple con valore di presente. In italiano si usa il congiuntivo presente («è ora che andiamo»).
alts: It is time we went home.
more: It's time we would go home.

items.wrong: I'd rather you don't smoke here.
items.right: I'd rather you didn't smoke here.
items.why: «I'd rather» + soggetto vuole il past simple. In italiano «preferirei che non fumassi» ha il congiuntivo imperfetto, ma si finisce per usare il presente.
alts: I would rather you didn't smoke here.
more: I'd rather you not to smoke here.

items.wrong: He denied to have stolen the money.
items.right: He denied having stolen the money.
items.why: «Deny» vuole il gerundio, non l'infinito. In italiano «negò di aver rubato» ha l'infinito.
alts: He denied stealing the money.
He denied that he had stolen the money.
more: He denied to steal the money.

items.wrong: I regret to tell her the truth.
items.right: I regret telling her the truth.
items.why: «Regret» + gerundio indica il rammarico per qualcosa già fatto; con l'infinito significa «mi dispiace dover dire». Nel significato di «mi pento» serve -ing.
more: I regret tell her the truth.

items.wrong: I lived in London for two years before to move to Paris.
items.right: I lived in London for two years before moving to Paris.
items.why: Dopo la preposizione «before» si usa il gerundio (o una frase intera). In italiano «prima di trasferirmi» ha l'infinito.
alts: I lived in London for two years before I moved to Paris.
more: I lived in London for two years before moved to Paris.

items.wrong: Not only he was late, but he also forgot the documents.
items.right: Not only was he late, but he also forgot the documents.
items.why: «Not only» a inizio frase richiede l'inversione ausiliare + soggetto.
more: Not only was he late, but he also forgetting the documents.

items.wrong: My boss is a person very demanding.
items.right: My boss is a very demanding person.
items.why: In inglese l'aggettivo va prima del nome. L'italiano «una persona molto esigente» lo mette dopo.
alts: My boss is very demanding.
more: My boss is a very demanding persons.

items.wrong: The unemployment is rising in southern Europe.
items.right: Unemployment is rising in southern Europe.
items.why: I sostantivi astratti in senso generale non vogliono l'articolo. In italiano «la disoccupazione» lo richiede.
alts: Unemployment is rising in Southern Europe.
more: Unemployment are rising in southern Europe.

items.wrong: The manager announced us that the office would close.
items.right: The manager told us that the office would close.
items.why: «Announce» vuole «to» davanti alla persona; con il complemento di persona diretto si usa «tell». L'italiano «ci ha annunciato» non ha preposizione.
alts: The manager announced to us that the office would close.
more: The manager told that the office would close to us.

items.wrong: Actually the economy is recovering.
items.right: Currently the economy is recovering.
items.why: «Actually» significa «in realtà», non «attualmente». Falso amico di «attualmente» (= currently).
alts: At the moment the economy is recovering.
At present the economy is recovering.
Currently, the economy is recovering.
more: Actually the economy are recovering.

items.wrong: I assisted to a very interesting lecture.
items.right: I attended a very interesting lecture.
items.why: «Assist» significa «aiutare»; per «assistere a» si usa «attend». Falso amico di «assistere».
alts: I went to a very interesting lecture.
more: I attended to a very interesting lecture.

items.wrong: We may eventually go to the cinema tonight.
items.right: We may possibly go to the cinema tonight.
items.why: «Eventually» significa «alla fine», non «eventualmente». Falso amico di «eventualmente» (= possibly, perhaps).
alts: We might possibly go to the cinema tonight.
We may well go to the cinema tonight.
We might go to the cinema tonight.
We may go to the cinema tonight.
more: We may possibly to go to the cinema tonight.

items.wrong: Our waiter was very educated.
items.right: Our waiter was very polite.
items.why: «Educated» vuol dire «istruito», non «educato». Falso amico di «educato» (= polite, well-mannered).
alts: Our waiter was very well-mannered.
Our waiter was very courteous.
more: Our waiter was very politely.

items.wrong: The film was a flop, so I was deluded.
items.right: The film was a flop, so I was disappointed.
items.why: «Deluded» significa «illuso, ingannato»; per «deluso» si usa «disappointed». Falso amico di «deluso».
more: The film was a flop, so I was disappointing.
